newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to boost shipping safety after Japan spill.
newsitem.headline: Russia to boost shipping safety after Japan spill.

text.p: Russia plans to improve the safety of ships using the Sea of Japan to prevent environmental disasters like to this month's oil spill from a sunken Russian tanker, Itar-Tass news agency said on Tuesday.
Tass quoted Russian Transport Minister Nikolai Tsakh as saying Russia and Japan would sign a new shipping agreement on safety issues and agree a document on joint measures to combat future disasters.
"These important documents exist and I think we will sign them in 1997," Tsakh said.

The 13,157-tonne Nakhodka, carrying 19,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil, broke in two in the Sea of Japan on January 2, causing Japan's worst oil spill disaster. The stern of the ship sank off the Japanese coast, and the bow was washed to the shore.

Tass said earlier that a Russian commission investigating the wreck of the Nakhodka determined that the tanker had been in good shape but that it sank after hitting a half-submerged ship in heavy seas.
The commission rejected suggestions that the shipwreck had been caused by a mine, by the age of the tanker or by a tidal wave.
